title: Additions Represented by Print Symbols

illustrates.quote: Represent a dash, hyphen, or special print sign (often unspaced) used to indicate the omission of a word or word part to which an addition is to be made by the braille hyphen.

print.printFeatures: A simple list of unnumbered entry items.

braille.notes: Left margin is 9 cells (stripped). The braille lines correspond exactly to the 5 printed items. Corrected per BANA errata/foreign-language changes (below): line 1's repetition symbol and the German unspaced-omission-plus-addition entries.

uncertain: The print symbol in 'der Spass, -̈e' is a hyphen with a diaeresis above it, transcribed as -̈ based on the braille modifier ⠸⠒ (diaeresis).
The print symbol in 'il-̂t' is a hyphen with a circumflex above it, transcribed as -̂ based on the braille modifier ⠸⠩ (circumflex).

printCorrections.evidence: references/_text/addendum_tobraille_formats__01232020_final_v3.txt / references/bana BRF for the new Example 21-38, and PDF page 579: the special print sign is ∝ (proportional-to), not ∞ (infinity); the two glyphs were confused in the original transcription.
PDF page 579: 'il' and the circumflex-marked hyphen are unspaced ('il-̂t'), not separated by a space as originally transcribed.

corrections.note: Line 1 is taken from the new Example 21-38 BRF: the repetition symbol ∝ is _"7, not a second plain hyphen. Lines 2 and 5 (der Tisch, —e / tu —ses) take the unspaced-omission-plus-addition form per 21.9.3a/b, following the BRF; because the German is uncontracted foreign material, no grade 1 indicator goes before 'e' (RUEB 13.2.2). Line 3 (der Spass, already writing its diaeresis modifier ^3 before the hyphen) and line 4 (exacto, -a) are unaffected — Emboss's own prepareMarks writes a combining-mark modifier AFTER a non-letter symbol today (wrong order, tracked separately as code fix K21); this gold correction only updates the expected braille, not the code.
